About.title: How Global Conflict Watch works
About.intro: Global Conflict Watch reports on the world's wars and crises in English and Urdu, and shows its working: every story lists its sources and what was checked.

mission.title: What we do
mission.body: We follow active conflicts and the diplomacy around them, and explain what changed, why it matters and what to watch next, without sensational language.

method.title: How a story is made
method.body: AI tools help us gather reports and draft stories. Nothing is published by a machine: an editor reads, corrects and approves every story and every translation before it goes live.

checks.title: How we check facts
checks.body: Names, titles, dates, figures and places are pulled out of each draft and checked against the sources. A story cannot be published while any fact is unresolved. Facts we cannot trace are removed.

languages.title: English and Urdu
languages.body: Stories are published in English and Urdu. The Urdu version is translated and then approved by the editor, just like the English one. If a translation is not ready, the story appears in English only.

corrections.title: Corrections
corrections.body: When we get something wrong we fix it and say so at the foot of the story. A form for reporting mistakes will be added here before launch.

independence.title: Independence
independence.body: We are funded by advertising and by readers' support. Advertisers have no say in what we report.

NotFound.title: Page not found
NotFound.body: We couldn't find that page. It may have moved, or the address may be wrong.
